clue.text: Ring back twice to express derision

indicators.note: twice says the reversed ring is written out two times over
back tells us to read the word for ring from right to left

parts.note: a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: Someone scornfully telephones a person again and again to mock them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call but is a noun, HOOP. 'back' turns HOOP into POOH and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something scornfully as nonsense is to sneer at it, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Fruit we handle clumsily more than once

indicators.note: more than once asks for the word for clumsy handling to be repeated

parts.note: to paw something is to handle it clumsily

explanation.surface: Some fruit that we keep fumbling with.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical fruit, another name for the papaya.

clue.text: Maybe no clear guide to the' future

parts.note: O is zero, nothing, so it stands for no

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Perhaps a prophecy offers no clear guidance about what is to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' gives O (nothing); 'Maybe' rearranges O with CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a prophetic shrine or priestess consulted for predictions of things to come.

clue.text: Water in which wild deer is reflected

parts.note: a pond is a body of water

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of deer running about in disorder

explanation.surface: A pond in which a wild deer's image appears mirrored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' looks like a mirror image in the water but means thought over. 'wild' scrambles DEER into ERED after POND.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflected here is a verb of thinking: considered carefully, mulled over.

clue.text: River in which there are dangerous eddies

indicators.note: in which there are says the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A river with treacherous whirlpools.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkshire river (also one in East Anglia), a common crossword waterway.

clue.text: Ebbing, as rank as the Dead Sea

indicators.note: ebbing means flowing back, so the little word as is read backwards

parts.note: a rank is a line, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: A receding tide smells as foul as the Dead Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' seems to mean foul-smelling but is a row, LINE; 'Ebbing' turns AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea is famously salty water, so something like it is salty.

clue.text: Mariner accustomed to being ill-treated

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
used, as in used to, means accustomed

explanation.surface: A sailor who has grown used to rough handling.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated badly or cruelly, a synonym of mistreated.

clue.text: No rating at sea, in the dark?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naval man of no rank, out at sea, feels uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like a sailor, fitting 'at sea', but the words are just letters for 'at sea' to scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark means lacking knowledge, uninformed.

clue.text: Yet inert characters can reform ——for ever!

indicators.note: can reform says the letters of the previous words may be put into a new form

explanation.surface: Even sluggish characters can change their ways permanently!
explanation.definitionFit: Endless time, which is what for ever amounts to.

clue.text: In front of writhing snakes, we exhibited lack of nerve

indicators.note: in front of places the word we before the other piece
writhing means twisting, so the letters of snakes squirm into a new order

explanation.surface: We showed cowardice before a mass of writhing snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A failing or frailty, here lack of courage.

clue.text: Fruity /Shakespearian role

definitions.meaning: a hard pear-shaped fruit used for jelly
Peter, the carpenter who directs the play in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.definitionFit: One word for a yellow orchard fruit and the surname of a mechanical in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Girl holding up companion's cup

indicators.note: in a down answer the girl holds the companion up, sitting beneath it

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order; the 's is is
Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl raises her friend's cup.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'holding up' puts the girl under CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet, especially the wine cup used at Communion.

clue.text: Retired successfully?

parts.note: retiring here means going to bed, and doing so successfully means one has dropped off

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has gone to bed and actually nodded off is sleeping.

clue.text: Land set aside for dams?

parts.note: dams are not reservoir walls but mother animals, here ewes, and the land is their grazing

explanation.definitionFit: A tract of pasture for grazing ewes and their flock.

clue.text: Play early Celtic air on a musical toy

indicators.note: play suggests the letters fooling around into a new order
early points to the opening letter of Celtic

explanation.surface: Performing an old Celtic tune on a toy instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early' gives C, which 'Play' rearranges with AIR and ON A.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, often a child's plaything.

clue.text: Through lace-work, cloth is visible

parts.note: per means through or by means of

indicators.note: work suggests the letters of lace are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Fabric can be seen through openwork lace.
explanation.definitionFit: A closely woven cotton fabric used for sheets.

clue.text: The problem with snipe

definitions.meaning: a tangle or difficulty, as in a tricky snarl to untie
a wading bird of the sandpiper family, related to the snipe

explanation.definitionFit: A hard tangle or difficulty, and also a shore bird of the sandpiper family akin to the snipe.

clue.text: In an agitated state? Take time off, to fish

indicators.note: take off says the letter for time is removed

parts.note: bristling means angrily agitated

explanation.surface: Agitated? Take a moment off to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-like fish, the sprat, canned as Norwegian sardines.

clue.text: Stretch a leg and note dislocation

indicators.note: dislocation means things knocked out of place, so these letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: Stretch your leg and you may notice a dislocated joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen or draw out, a synonym of stretch.

clue.text: Rousing game in foreign city

definitions.meaning: game birds are flushed when driven from cover
a Dutch port, Vlissingen in Dutch

explanation.definitionFit: Driving birds from cover for shooters, and the English name of the Dutch port of Vlissingen.

clue.text: Baker's turnover

definitions.meaning: a baker's product, a small loaf of bread
a turn over, as of a vessel or aircraft ...

explanation.definitionFit: A small bread bun made by a baker, and the action of turning over sideways.

clue.text: The noise? It's the sound of geese crossing the river

indicators.note: crossing says the geese's call goes over, around, the river

parts.note: geese cackle

explanation.surface: A noise is heard: geese honking as they fly across the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of sharp snapping sounds, a type of noise.

clue.text: Mongrel carrying article, for sport

indicators.note: carrying means the dog has the article inside it

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A mongrel dog fetches something for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is not a game: in biology a sport is an animal or plant that differs strikingly from its parents.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a sport is an offspring showing an abrupt variation, a freak of nature.

clue.text: Girl from the naval base

definitions.meaning: a harbour for yachts and pleasure boats

explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and a dock for pleasure craft.

clue.text: It takes fourteen pounds, to come to bad end, high on drugs

parts.note: a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

indicators.note: end points to the last letter of bad

explanation.surface: Someone who weighs more and more comes to a bad end, high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds; 'bad end' gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for intoxicated by drugs.

clue.text: Assured of New Guinea's reform

indicators.note: reform means the letters are formed again in a new order

parts.note: the possessive is read as guineas, its S kept

explanation.surface: Confident of political reform in New Guinea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Guinea' looks like one place, but New gives only N; 'reform' rearranges N with GUINEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Confident and optimistic, a synonym of assured.

clue.text: With doubt? Seek information from a good book

parts.note: to ask is to seek information
NT is the New Testament, part of the Good Book

explanation.surface: Doubtful? Look things up in a trusted book.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking sideways, hence suspiciously or doubtfully, a variant of askance.

clue.text: Petty-officer heading for a hip joint

parts.note: a cox or coxswain may be a petty officer steering a boat

explanation.surface: A naval officer is off to have a hip operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' links COX to A; COXA is the anatomical name for the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin anatomical term for the hip or hip joint.

clue.text: Upright character to veto poster introduced into state capital

parts.note: the letter I is a single upright stroke

indicators.note: introduced into means one piece is slipped inside the other

parts.note: to ban is to veto
an ad, advertisement, is a poster

explanation.surface: An upstanding figure vetoes putting up posters in a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright character' sounds like an honest person but is the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Nigerian city, the capital of Oyo State.

clue.text: Cheat an underling to gain power

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
a minion is an underling

explanation.surface: Swindle a subordinate to seize control.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovereignty or control, a synonym of power.

clue.text: A quarter got the improved version

indicators.note: an improved version is the original remade, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone receives a quarter of the improved edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter of a city where a minority group lives, often segregated.

clue.text: Sentry joins vehicle heading for the front line

indicators.note: joins says the sentry links up after the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a guard is a sentry

explanation.surface: A soldier climbs aboard a truck bound for the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The foremost position of an advancing army, its leading part.
